subject: WarmStart economics confirmation & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@acmehealth.com>, Aaron Cho <aaron.cho@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: WarmStart economics confirmation & next steps

Hi Priya / Aaron —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned on the cost levers and next steps. I’ve attached a short workbook (acme_warmstart_volumes_20270109.xlsx) and our draft estimate (redwood_estimate_v2.pdf).

What we heard on the call:
- Monthly expected traffic: ~420M tokens (production) + ~60M tokens for QA/staging; monthly peak day ~22M tokens.
- Target unit economics: you called out a target neighborhood of ~$300–$400 per 1M effective tokens (post-caching).
- Typical conversation pattern: many repeated prefixes (form data + user context) for guided intake flows. Team indicated reuse could be material.
- Model candidate: redwood-2-xl (or a quantized v2-xl variant) for initial pilot.

Key pricing assumptions we used in the attached estimate:
- Baseline model cost (no caching): $1.10 per 1k tokens in our hosted model profile, translating to $1100 per 1M tokens before optimizations.
- Prefix (warm) cache: we modeled hit rates at 0%, 30%, and 50% to show sensitivity. Effective price falls materially as hit rate improves because cached prefixes avoid repeated forward passes.
- Effective $/1M tokens (example):
  - 0% cache hit: ~$1,100
  - 30% cache hit: ~$770
  - 50% cache hit: ~$550
- Additional levers: batching (savings depend on latency SLOs), quantized model variants (~20–30% lower per-token cost), and a possible committed capacity discount for Dedicated.

Open asks for you (to confirm the estimate and help us finalize pricing):
1) Can you confirm the monthly token baseline and peak-day token numbers? The workbook has our best-guess numbers you can edit.
2) What range of prefix reuse (hit rate) do you expect from your existing logs? Even a rough % is very helpful.
3) What’s the budget target you want us to aim for (net $/1M tokens after caching) for a pilot vs production?

Proposed next steps:
- You update the attached workbook with any corrected volumes and share sample logs via the Drive link above (we’ll treat them as PII-minimized).
- We run a quick warmstart-sensitivity run and return a tightened pilot quote within 48 hours.
- Book a 30-minute follow-up next week to lock the pilot scope.

I’m looping Laura on this thread to align on pilot credit/discount options.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — really helpful recap. A few clarifications and answers below:

- Volumes: the 420M/month number is our best estimate for production after launch (we expect a staged ramp over 3 months). QA/staging is closer to 50–70M/month. Peak-day of ~20–25M tokens sounds right for our busiest intake day.
- Prefix reuse: from a quick sample of our logs, the guided intake flows show roughly 38–42% reuse of repeated prefixes (users hit the same form templates). For full conversational features reuse drops — maybe ~15–20% overall.
- Budget: for an initial pilot we’re targeting an effective rate of $250–$350 per 1M tokens post-caching. For production we’d be comfortable in the $300–$400 neighborhood, assuming measured hit rates and SLA.

We attached a small excerpt of sanitized interaction logs to the Drive link — should help you refine the warmstart hit-rate model.

For next steps — please share a pilot quote that shows: (a) expected effective $/1M at our stated hit rates (38–42% on intake flows), (b) what the cost would look like if we opt for the quantized model variant, and (c) suggested guardrails (max latency/throughput) for achieving the batch/caching savings. Happy to do a 30-minute follow-up next Tue or Wed.

Thanks —
Priya Shah
Head of Product, Acme Health

Hi all — quick technical-economic note and proposed follow-up time.

Sensitivity highlights (back-of-envelope based on our serving profile for redwood-2-xl):
- Baseline run cost (no cache, full-precision): ~$1,100 per 1M tokens.
- Quantized v2-xl (8-bit q): ~25% lower compute cost -> baseline ~$825 per 1M.
- WarmStart cache: each cached prefix avoids the initial encoder/decoder passes for the repeated prefix portion. At 40% prefix hit on intake flows we see an additional ~32% reduction in effective tokens billed (depends on average prefix length).

Combined examples (approx):
- Quantized + 40% warm hit => effective ~$560 per 1M tokens.
- Quantized + 50% warm hit => effective ~$440 per 1M tokens.

If Acme’s intake flows (where reuse is ~40–42%) represent ~60% of your total tokens, then portfolio-level effective $/1M could reach mid-$300s once batching and committed capacity discounts are applied. That gets us into your production target range.

Latency/throughput note:
- To preserve sub-400ms median response on intake flows while retaining batching benefits, we recommend a conservative batching window (10–25ms) plus a separate low-latency pool for critical flows. We’ll outline the exact SLOs in the pilot doc.

Next steps I’ll take (deliverables by EOD Monday):
1) A short sensitivity table (40% / 50% / 0% warm hit) with quantized vs FP numbers and effective $/1M at the portfolio level.
2) A recommended pilot configuration (batch windows, cache TTLs, model variant) and expected SLO tradeoffs.
3) A draft pilot quote showing a 6-week timeline, optional performance tranche, and a proposed pilot credit amount.

Proposed follow-up call: Tue Jan 12, 10:00 AM PT — please confirm and I’ll send a calendar invite.

—Sergio
